facts.fact: Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB, lists CAMIX Douala in Cameroon with 10 member ASNs and 40 Gbps cumulative port capacity, 9 of 10 peering at the route server (data as of August 2026).
Akamai Technologies (AS20940, content network) is listed as a member of CAMIX Douala with a 4 Gbps port, peering at the route server, per PeeringDB via Internet Society Pulse.
Of CAMIX Douala's 10 members, 3 are registered abroad: PCH AS3856 and PCH AS42 (United States) and Akamai Technologies (Netherlands), per PeeringDB via Internet Society Pulse.

systems.country_label: Cameroon Internet Exchange Point - CAMIX Douala

facts.fact: CAMIX states its third point of presence, at the ST-DIGITAL data centre (carrier hotel), has been in service since 1 July with two members connected, INK and ST-DIGITAL; the article is dated 7 April 2026 yet says 1 July, year not restated, taken as 2026.
CAMIX says its interconnection infrastructure already had two operational sites, a Douala PoP at CAMTEL Bepanda and a Yaounde PoP at the CAMPOST data centre, before the third PoP at ST-DIGITAL.

note: Not facts: SANCFIS and Afri-IX connecting, and talks with Orange, MTN and CAMTEL, are in preparation only.

facts.fact: CAMIX's own homepage reports 12+ active members, 3 points of presence, 100G Ethernet circuit capacity and 1 ms local latency; undated living page whose latest item is July 2026, so as_of is that month.
CAMIX lists Google Global Cache and an Akamai cache as additional services served directly from CAMIX, per its own homepage.
CAMIX lists points of presence in Yaounde (CAMPOST data centre) and in Douala (CAMTEL Bepanda and ST-Digital), per its own homepage.

note: Forward notice of a peering forum in Yaounde co-hosted with CAMIX; states nothing on an exchange's service, traffic, content or reach.
Event announcement for a Yaounde peering forum; no statement on any Cameroon exchange point's operation.

facts.fact: ST DIGITAL says its DLA01 data centre in Douala houses DOUALA-IX, an open, neutral peering point whose members include AFRI-IX Telecom, CAMIX NAP, INQ Digital Cameroon SA, Opex Network and SWECOM; it holds IXP OIX-1 certification from the Open-IX Association (no date given for the service, so the 2024-09-11 publication date is used; no member count given).

note: One service fact; no traffic figure, content network, second city or foreign members named.
Names KIXP, NAPAfrica, JINX, IXPN Lagos and others only for Starlink gateways in other countries; Cameroon appears only as a restricted Starlink market, so no exchange fact for CMR.

facts.fact: Camtel staff say an exchange point run by CAMIX brings together several players, but is still embryonic.
CAMIX says at least eight operators/ISPs are connected to its exchange points at Yaoundé and Douala.
CAMIX says Akamai servers have arrived at its Douala exchange point and are in production.
CAMIX says its exchange operates points in two cities, Yaoundé and Douala.
ISOC Pulse's IXP Tracker lists 3 exchange points in Cameroon with 16 of 31 networks peering.
CAMIX's own membership guide describes ISPs, hosts and operators exchanging traffic locally through its route-server at its points of presence, settlement-free.
CAMIX's guide says members get access to Google Global Cache, an Akamai cache to be reactivated shortly, OpenDNS and NTP hosted at the exchange.
CAMIX's guide says member ports are provisioned at its points of presence in Douala or Yaounde.
The African IXP Association's undated list of exchange points, retrieved 2026-11-09, names for Cameroon: CAMIX, Douala and Yaounde.
The African IXP Association's undated list, retrieved 2026-11-09, places Cameroon's exchange points in more than one city: Douala and Yaounde.
